newsitem.title: USA: CFTC's Dial warns against excessive deregulation.
newsitem.headline: CFTC's Dial warns against excessive deregulation.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission commissioner Joseph Dial said Thursday that the CFTC has serious concerns about the significant deregulation of U.S. futures exchanges proposed in legislation to amend the Commodity Exchange Act.

In a paper prepared for delivery to the National Grain and Feed Association, Dial said that certain provisions of the bill, called the "promarket exemptions," would deregulate 90 percent of current exchange trading volume and "creat U.S. exchanges with less government regulation than any other futures exchanges in the world."
Dial disputed arguments by U.S. exchanges that deregulation is needed to meet competition from foreign exchanges and from over-the-counter (OTC) transactions.

He said that although the U.S. market share of futures trading has dropped, the U.S. trading volume has increased more than 20 times in the last two decades, and that very little offshore trading is in direct competition with U.S. markets.

Dial also argued against the OTC defense, saying that futures exchanges create a "concentration of risk" not present in OTC transactions and could more seriously threaten the economy if anything went wrong.

"A default on an OTC contract primarily affects only the two principals," said Dial. "A default on a futures market can hurt hundreds of producers, processors and other buinesses that depend on those markets for hedging, and millions of consumers who -- whether they know it or not -- depend on them for price basing."
